title: Assignment 21 · Mistake, impracticability, and frustration
summary: Mistake, impracticability, and frustration. Assigned readings and principal cases for this class.
notes:
Stees v. Leonard: A builder’s undertaking to erect and complete a building placed the burden of overcoming the site’s quicksand conditions on the builder under the court’s strict reading of the contract.

Renner v. Kehl: A shared material mistake about water needed for jojoba cultivation justified rescission, but restitution did not reimburse all development expenditure regardless of benefit to the sellers.

Taylor v. Caldwell: The accidental destruction of the particular music hall essential to the planned concerts excused both sides from future performance.

Transatlantic Financing Corp. v. United States: Closure of the Suez Canal did not make an available, more expensive Cape route commercially impracticable on this record, and the shipowner could not add the extra expense to its agreed price.

Krell v. Henry: Cancellation of the coronation procession defeated the shared foundation for hiring particular viewing rooms, excusing payment of the remaining charge.

Additional assigned materials: Force majeure clause.
